newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Future HK government to finalise vote law soon.
newsitem.headline: Future HK government to finalise vote law soon.

text.p: A senior aide to future Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Tuesday the post-colonial government would decide next month on laws governing elections to the first legislature under Chinese rule.
China has decided to scrap the first-past-the-post electoral system introduced by the British-led administration in 1995 after it takes back control of Hong Kong at midnight on June 30.
Tung has been given a choice for the 1998 Legislative Council election between a multi-seat single vote system and proportional representation.

A provisional legislature handpicked by Beijing will replace the current elected body on July 1, sitting until the first election under Chinese rule can be held. It is expected the election will take place in the first half of next year.

The pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong and analysts have said both proposed models were intended to slash the chances of the Democrats, who won most of the 20 directly elected seats in the outgoing 60-strong Legislative Council.
The remaining 40 seats were decided through indirect election.
But Tung aide Sir Sze-yuen Chung said both the proportional representation and multi-seat single vote system were fairer than the current first-past-the-post voting method.
"The method for the direct election must be fair and just... The importance is that it must be fair and just," Chung told reporters.
